DV-002.how: Severity is no longer carried by hue alone anywhere on the dashboard. Every verdict pill now renders through one pillHtml() helper that emits three redundant channels: a band WORD ('ok' / 'warn' / 'critical' / 'no data'), a band MARK whose SHAPE differs per band (filled circle, up triangle, filled square, en dash), and the colour. The critical band additionally takes a 2px border where the others take 1px. The false-positives tile, which was also colour-only, appends the band word to its key line. The band vocabulary lives in BAND_WORD / BAND_MARK so a fourth band cannot be added colour-only.

VD-009.how: There is now one token set. The block that was 9 tokens in panel.html and a different 15 in dashboard.html (and a third variant in debug.html) is a single block, byte for byte identical in all three pages, grouped and commented, naming panel.html as the source of truth. It gains --sunk, --faint, --crit, --accent-soft, --edge, --on-accent and the three type tokens the panel did not have. Every hardcoded literal named in the row is gone: the three color:#fff on var(--accent) go through --on-accent (defined #FFFFFF in light and #0E1116 in dark, so the 2.71:1 dark-theme case is a token a contrast audit can see), .cardframe iframe's #fff becomes var(--raised) and .proof img's #000 becomes var(--ink), so both follow the theme flip. Every font stack literal in panel.html is replaced by var(--display) / var(--body) / var(--mono): 3 body, 8 display and 4 mono occurrences. A separate shared .css file was rejected deliberately, not overlooked: the pages are served by lib/server.js:607 with the control token injected, a <link rel=stylesheet> cannot carry that header, so a shared file would need a new route plus an entry in isTokenExempt (lib/auth.js:121) and therefore a daemon restart, and the running daemon must not be restarted. The comment in each file says so and says to paste the block.
